leave.why: a winter-trained model did not carry to the summer window: in the winter half the Americas' clubs (their main window) lose players and Europe's keep them; in the summer half it is the other way round

meta.method: Chance of moving: the share of players like him who left their club in the latest transfer window of the same kind (last winter for the coming winter), by league and role (regular, rotation, fringe; on loan by region), from Sofascore's club transfer lists and player histories and our line-ups. It is a base rate, not a player-level forecast: our player-level model was tested on a held-out window and did not beat the base rate, because the winter and summer windows move different players (the Americas' main window is our winter, Europe's our summer). A region-aware version is being forward-tested on this winter's window. If he moves, how (transfer, free, loan, loan ending, release) and where (same league, a stronger or weaker one, outside our leagues) come from models that beat the base rates on the held-out window. Targets rank players by their chance of joining the club: availability x a model of which clubs movers join (league, region, strength, quality against the club's players, the club's expected departures at the position), which beat availability alone on the held-out window. No contract data: Transfermarkt's, Spotrac's and similar sites' terms forbid reuse, and Sofascore's contract end dates are a snapshot of today only, so no model here can learn from them. Windows are halves of the year (May-October, November-April); every league's registration period falls inside its half.
